Melos searched along the banks, but there was no other way across. He stepped into the water. The current swept his feet away. Muddy water filled his mouth. env_rows.canonical: Beyond the river, attackers blocked the road. One grabbed his arm. Another swung a stick. Melos struck out, broke free, and stumbled past them. Their angry shouts followed him, but he did not look back. By afternoon, pain filled every step. Then his legs gave way. He lay with his face against the earth. The city was still far away. He could not reach it. He could not even stand. He could stay here. No one would find him before sunset. His friend would die, but he would live. For one terrible moment, the thought brought relief. Then he remembered those warm fingers around his hand.

env_rows.canonical: This news feels like a short play in 3 acts. The first act was 20%. Act 2 brought an unexpected turn. Act 3 was an unexpected move in oil prices. The curtain rose on July 13. At 10:16 a.m., Trump posted that the United States would seek a 20% charge on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The aim was to recover the cost of US efforts to keep the strait safe. But 20% was not a finished system. The post did not say who would pay, how the money would be collected, or what legal basis would support it. For the moment, only a large number stood at center stage. The number stayed at center stage for about a day. Then the story took a sharp turn.
